name: Cal McNair

views.text: When the window opens, we spend to win now.
I sit in on the head-coach search myself; I learned that the hard way.
A young quarterback on a rookie deal is the time to add stars around him.
We embrace the expectations of being a contender.
A coach who does not show progress in year one may not get a year two.
Guaranteed money is fine when it buys proven production.

signatures: speaks alongside family members at team events
want: Turn the Texans into a perennial AFC contender while the young core is cheap (medium).
fear: Wasting a rookie-contract window and returning to the lean years (medium).
voice: Polite, earnest, family-centered; speaks in team-mission phrases. Lets his general manager handle the detail and talks about expectations and community.

evidence.summary: After firing two head coaches after one season each, McNair broke from his family's laissez-faire style by taking part in the whole search that produced DeMeco Ryans.
The McNairs discussed an aggressive 2024 offseason (Stefon Diggs trade, Danielle Hunter and Joe Mixon deals) and said they wanted to win now and embraced expectations.
NFL owners unanimously approved Cal McNair as the Texans' principal owner, succeeding his mother Janice.

review.notes: Thin coverage: two to four sources found by web search (2026-11-06); sliders mostly left at 5; a few publication dates are taken from the news cycle the article covers. Draft for JR to check.
